request.what: Reduce the Cardano protocol parameter committeeMinSize from 7 to 5.

claims.claim: The proposal changes the minimum Constitutional Committee size parameter, committeeMinSize, from 7 to 5.
The current Constitutional Committee comprises 7 members, equal to the current committeeMinSize setting of 7.

If Constitutional Committee membership drops below committeeMinSize, governance actions requiring Constitutional Committee approval become ineligible for ratification, including Parameter Changes, Constitution Updates, Treasury Withdrawals, and Hard Forks.
Reducing committeeMinSize to 5 would provide an operational buffer so governance can continue if one or two members retire or their terms expire, assuming a current 7-member body.

The proposal depends temporally on enactment of another live Parameter Change governance action for Plutus cost model settings, but the document states there is no technical interaction between the parameter changes.
The proposal states that it does not directly affect the current number of Committee members and does not imply that reducing Constitutional Committee size is desired.
At a Constitutional Committee size of 5 with a 2/3 threshold, 4 constitutional votes meet the threshold and 2 unconstitutional votes can prevent the threshold.
The proposal states it underwent technical review through the Parameter Committee Parameter Change Process and references the Cardano Forum PCP-005 discussion.
The document states the change satisfies guardrails requiring committeeMinSize to be non-negative, at least 3, and no more than 10.

The reversion plan says returning committeeMinSize to 7 is possible if there are at least 7 Constitutional Committee members, but would immediately halt governance if fewer than 7 members were present at reversion.

summary: The document requests a non-treasury parameter change to lower committeeMinSize from 7 to 5, primarily to reduce governance inoperability risk while acknowledging changed voting dynamics and a conditional reversion risk.
